installer: change postinst to run inside the installed path All the postinst logic manually adds the specified path to the prefix of the tools it runs in order to find the right binary. But we run into the problem of running dynamic programs against a different runtime. To work around this, we statically linked things, but that's problematic: - we sometimes forget to statically link programs - it's hard to know what all programs actually need to be - shell scripts make this problem much worse - mixing of static & dynamic causes disk bloat - static linkage bleeds into other targets too (firmware updater/initramfs) Lets change the postinst code so that it runs in the target root as any other chroot. All of our dynamic linkage issues go away as a result. security_AccountsBaseline: Read from rootfs and allow board baselines This is a two-part change: - When testing on Lakitu, read /etc/passwd and /etc/group from the rootfs. On Lakitu a tmpfs is overlayed on top of /etc and the google-accounts-daemon adds dynamic users/groups that are not easy to predict from the test. This is true especially when VMTest is run from a GCE builder, in which case the daemon adds local users for all Editors/Owners of the GCE project the builder resides in. - Allow board baselines to override the default baseline. For example, on Lakitu the group 'tty' has a different list of users than that of Freon. While this can and needs to be changed, we may have some other valid cases like this in the future. This change makes the baseline parsing logic board independent. BUG=chromium:753016 TEST=lakitu-pre-cq on both baremetal and GCE builders Change-Id: I78526e80983aa506fc66b0e2e631a2e4b58c6139 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/699194 Commit-Ready: Daniel Wang <wonderfly@google.com> Tested-by: Daniel Wang <wonderfly@google.com> Reviewed-by: Jorge Lucangeli Obes <jorgelo@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>
